runs.head: bfb4ac7653f6
runs.summary: Ran all six Done Contract checks (pass), diffed the vendored engine, pack, ruleset, workflow, template and AGENTS.md against the framework at the SOURCE commit (identical; settings rules match the seed; the framework's own 143 tests pass), and probed the guard by hand. Then exercised claim, save, the stop and pulse hooks, takeover and review in a scratch project with a local remote: the claim rules behave as described, but a review run that starts ten minutes after the ticket's last event leaves the branch diverged from the remote, and the new engine revives ticket 8.

findings.claim: `run` reads `head` before `keep_alive`, which commits and pushes a `saved` event when the ticket's last event is at least `save_minutes` old; after the reviewer, `git reset --hard head` moves the branch back behind that pushed commit. The review run is then committed on the old head and its push is refused as a non-fast-forward, so the run never reaches the remote and every later push of the branch is refused too (sequence: a ticket in `reviewing`, `rail advance` more than ten minutes after its last event, such as a session coming back from a pause or after an invalid-output review).
findings.check: A test that runs `rail advance` on a ticket in `reviewing` whose last event is older than `[claim] save_minutes`, and asserts that the local branch and the remote branch have the same tip afterwards.

evidence.command: Scratch clone with a bare remote, MEDIUM ticket 2 shipped, first review run invalid (state reviewing). Then `python3 later.py advance 2` (rail with minutes_since() answering 11 more) and `git rev-parse --short` / `git log --oneline -3` of the local and remote branch; then a plain `rail advance 2`.

findings.claim: With this engine ticket 8 is no longer `merged`: its contract pull request #11 was merged with no ship, so it becomes `new` with owner `agent` (CONTRACT_MERGED). After ticket 9 merges, the next `rail next` records the merge as the owner's approval of ticket 8 and hands an agent the same contract ticket 9 just delivered; nothing in the change drops ticket 8 or says a person must.
findings.check: After the change, `rail status --json` lists no ticket with owner `agent` whose Done Contract equals that of a merged ticket; here, ticket 8 is dropped before or with the merge.

runs.head: 35d40d342db7
runs.summary: Re-reviewed the whole change. All six Done Contract checks pass. `.rail/engine`, `.rail/packs`, `.rail/ruleset.json`, the workflow and the ticket template are byte-identical to the framework at the commit in `.rail/SOURCE`, and that commit's own 145 tests pass. `.claude/settings.json` has the seed's rules. F1 is fixed (the sign of life is written before the head is read) and F2 is fixed (`rail status` shows ticket 8 dropped, with a `rail drop 8` mark on `rail/ids`). About 40 guard probes found one remaining fail-open, reported below with one wording mismatch; neither blocks the merge.

findings.claim: A `cd` the guard can't follow is recognised only when `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` is the first word of a simple command. After `cd OTHER_REPO &&`, a `cd -` inside a brace group, after `then`, or after `!` is missed, so the push to `main` or `gh pr merge` that follows is judged as the other repository's and allowed. This is the sweep's F1 case in another spelling, and `docs/guards.md` says whatever can't be followed is judged as this project's.
findings.check: A guard test that expects deny for `cd OTHER && { cd -; git push origin main; }`, `cd OTHER && if true; then cd -; fi && git push origin main` and `cd OTHER && ! cd - && git push origin main`, where OTHER is another git repository.

evidence.command: Piped each command line to `RAIL_CLOUD=0 .rail/bin/rail hook guard` as a Bash PreToolUse event with cwd set to the ticket's worktree; /tmp/other is another git repository on branch main.

findings.claim: The ticket's Why says work a session abandoned is resumed after an hour, but the engine copied in resumes it after `[claim] stale_minutes` = 30 (config.py default, and the ticket's own Look at says 30 minutes). The Why becomes the pull request's description, so the owner is told twice the real limit.

runs.head: 95399c02bb76
runs.summary: All six Done Contract checks pass, and `.rail/engine`, the consult pack, `ruleset.json`, the workflow and the settings rules match the framework at the commit in `.rail/SOURCE` (the framework's 146 tests pass on that engine). F1 to F4 are fixed. Driving the copied engine in scratch clones with a bare remote found two advisory problems: a crash when `rail` runs with no session id, and a save hook that pushes a reviewer's scratch files when it fires during a review.

findings.claim: `_save_note` reads the cache with key `session or ""`, so with no `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` it opens the directory `rail/cache/hooks/` and `rail next` dies with a traceback. Sequence: any Claude session has started in the clone (the SessionStart hook creates that folder), then `rail next --ticket 1` or a bare `rail next` runs from a plain terminal or another agent; the claim is committed before the crash.
findings.check: A test that runs the session-start hook with a session id, then `rail next --ticket NN` with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID unset, and expects exit 0 with an IMPLEMENT brief.

evidence.command: Scratch clone with a bare remote: `rail add`, `rail next` (session-a), `rail hook session-start` with session_id session-a, then `env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u RAIL_TICKET rail next --ticket 1 --json`
evidence.output:
rc 1
  File ".../engine/rail/table.py", line 137, in _save_note
    if f.project.cache_read("hooks", f.project.session or ""):
  File ".../engine/rail/project.py", line 224, in cache_read
    with open(path) as f:
IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.../t1/a/.git/rail/cache/hooks/'

findings.claim: The save hooks don't know a review is running: when the session's PostToolUse hook fires while its own `rail advance` is inside a review (a parallel tool call, or advance run in the background), `save_work` commits and pushes the reviewer's in-scope scratch files. The review's `git reset --hard head` then moves the branch back behind that push, so the `review` commit never reaches the remote and local and remote stay diverged (the same end state as F1).
findings.check: A test whose review command writes a file inside scope_paths and sleeps, runs `rail hook pulse` for the same session meanwhile, and asserts the remote branch has no scratch file and equals the local branch after advance.

evidence.command: Scratch clone with a bare remote, MEDIUM ticket 1, review command `echo scratch > src/scratch.py; sleep 6; python3 fake_reviewer.py`; `rail advance 1` in one thread, `rail hook pulse` (same session) 4 s later; then `git log --oneline` of the local and remote branch, and `rail advance 1` again
